security.reason: The wave changes typed planning contracts and provenance/cache identity but adds no provider credentials, new network endpoint, secret storage, physical generation, or production capability grant.

conflicts.originalConflict: A historical F04 payload dependency can appear to imply F03 -> F04, while canonical FloorRegistry topology remains F02 -> (F03 || F04) -> F05.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Preserve the canonical parallel topology and treat F04 contract reconciliation as a separate future change.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: Wave 5 does not serialize F04 behind F03.

conflicts.originalConflict: External media-generation systems often encode references and controls with provider-specific paths or model parameters.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Represent logical entity identity, typed conditioning and dependency lineage in provider-neutral F03 contracts; keep resolution/execution downstream.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: ReferenceBinding and ConditioningSpec are declarative only.

conflicts.originalConflict: Runtime asset UUID changes can otherwise prevent deterministic dependency-aware cache invalidation across surgical regeneration.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Record dependency-node fingerprints on dependency edges and recompute them in sequence order during regeneration.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: Only the affected dependency subgraph changes fingerprints; unrelated branches remain reusable.
